# I switched my local LLM setup to Ollama's new MLX engine, and my Mac suddenly feels twice as fast

I have been using Ollama to run local LLMs on my Mac, and it has been working just fine. However, my Mac's overall performance took a hit because [local LLMs are resource-hungry](https://www.xda-developers.com/the-biggest-thing-holding-local-ai-back-isnt-model-quality-its-friction/). I have a MacBook Air M5 with 16GB of RAM. It's probably not the most powerful machine for this kind of workload, but it's been good enough to run models with fewer than 7 billion parameters.

That changed completely after I upgraded to Ollama's new MLX engine. I'm seeing massive performance improvements. Everything feels much more responsive, and inference is almost twice as fast now.

If you're already [running local LLMs](https://www.xda-developers.com/tested-local-llm-different-tools-and-only-one-unleashed-its-potential/) on a Mac through Ollama, this is one of the biggest upgrades since Apple Silicon became a serious inference platform. The latest MLX engine changes how models are represented, how memory is used, and how agent workflows are cached, which also has a massive impact on [coding assistants like Claude Code](https://www.xda-developers.com/found-a-free-open-source-alternative-to-claude-code/), OpenClaw, Aider, and other multi-agent setups.

#### [I finally found a local LLM I actually want to use for coding](https://www.xda-developers.com/finally-found-local-llm-want-use-coding/)

Qwen3-Coder-Next is a great model, and it's even better with Claude Code as a harness.

## The MLX engine finally makes better use of Apple Silicon

### It puts Apple Silicon to good use

Most local LLM users already know that Apple Silicon performs surprisingly well despite having relatively modest hardware. My MacBook Air M5 with 16GB of RAM handled smaller models without many issues, but the experience always came with trade-offs. Running a local model often slowed down everything else on the system.

Ollama's new MLX engine changes that by relying much more heavily on Apple's own MLX framework and unified memory architecture. As you know, Apple Silicon lets both the CPU and GPU share the same memory pool instead of treating them as separate pieces of hardware. The updated engine makes much better use of that design, reducing unnecessary memory movement during inference.

The improvements go beyond better memory management. Ollama now combines several GPU operations into larger Metal kernels via MLX's just-in-time compiler, reducing inference overhead. The engine also improves GPU-backed sampling, allowing tokens to generate much faster than before. Ollama claims the updated engine can deliver roughly 20% higher output speed than the previous Q4_K_M implementation, which matches what I noticed during daily use.

My own workflow never revolves around running large benchmark prompts. I usually spend my time asking programming questions, generating scripts, or testing automation ideas. Those workloads consist of many short requests throughout the day, and each one now feels more responsive.

## Smaller models now produce better responses

### Finally

Performance improvements usually receive the most attention, but I think the quality improvements matter just as much. Ollama's updated MLX engine now supports NVIDIA's model-optimized NVFP4 quantization format. Quantization reduces the memory required to run a model, but it also removes some information from the original weights. Lower memory usage usually comes at the cost of lower output quality.

NVFP4 reduces that compromise significantly. According to Ollama's own measurements with Gemma 4 12B, the new format reduces quality loss by roughly half compared to the widely used Q4_K_M format while maintaining similar memory requirements. The benchmark shows lower perplexity than Q4_K_M, which generally indicates that the model behaves much closer to its original BF16 version.

My Mac cannot comfortably run extremely large models, so I spend most of my time using smaller ones. Better quantization enables smaller models to produce stronger results without requiring additional hardware. That's a meaningful upgrade for anyone using a MacBook Air or another Apple Silicon system with limited memory.

I now notice that the generated code follows instructions more consistently, and follow-up prompts require fewer corrections than before. Responses also remain coherent over longer conversations, reducing the time spent rewriting prompts.

## Coding agents benefit even more

### Ollama redesigned agent workflows

The feature that surprised me the most has nothing to do with raw inference speed. Ollama also redesigned how its MLX engine handles cached model state during agent workflows. That's a big deal because coding assistants constantly resend huge amounts of context back to the model. Every tool call includes the system prompt, tool definitions, previous conversation history, and recently loaded files.

### Save on Mac performance upgrades: deals for faster AI workflows

Traditional prefix caching only works while every request continues directly from the previous one. Modern coding agents rarely behave that way because they frequently branch into sub-agents, retry failed requests, or remove reasoning tokens from the visible conversation. Those changes normally force the model to process the same context repeatedly, even though most of it never changes.

Ollama addresses that problem with a new snapshot system. Instead of relying entirely on prefix caching, the engine stores reusable model states at important points during a conversation. Separate agent sessions can resume from those saved states instead of rebuilding everything from the beginning. Thinking models also benefit because snapshots preserve a useful state before reasoning tokens disappear from the conversation history.

### Ollama is a lot better now

The new update improves everything you use local LLMs for, whether it's chatting with a model or using it as a coding assistant. My own local workflows feel much quicker because repeated tool calls no longer spend as much time rebuilding context. Faster response times, combined with better output quality, make the new MLX engine one of the most worthwhile upgrades I have made to my local AI setup.

#### Ollama

Ollama is a platform to download and run various open-source large language models (LLM) on your local computer.

#### [Ollama is still the easiest way to start local LLMs, but it's the worst way to keep running them](https://www.xda-developers.com/ollama-easiest-way-start-local-llms-worst-keep-running/)

Ollama is great for getting you started... just don't stick around.

- [AI tools](https://www.xda-developers.com/ai-tools/)
- [AI](https://www.xda-developers.com/tag/ai/)

#### [A Microsoft researcher built a goat-powered LLM in Age of Empires II to prove it's not sentient](https://www.xda-developers.com/a-microsoft-researcher-built-an-llm-in-age-of-empires-using-goats-to-prove-its-not-sentient/)

#### [High-VRAM GPUs aren't the future of local AI — unified memory and Mixture of Experts models are](https://www.xda-developers.com/high-vram-gpus-future-local-ai-unified-memory-mixture-experts/)

#### [I ran Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 for the same local tasks, and one pulled miles ahead](https://www.xda-developers.com/ran-gemma-4-and-qwen-35-for-same-local-tasks-one-pulled-ahead/)

# 我把本機 LLM 環境切到 Ollama 新的 MLX 引擎後，我的 Mac 突然感覺快了一倍

我一直用 Ollama 在 Mac 上跑本機 LLM，而且用起來其實還不錯。不過，我的 Mac 整體效能因此受到影響，因為[本機 LLM 很吃資源](https://www.xda-developers.com/the-biggest-thing-holding-local-ai-back-isnt-model-quality-its-friction/)。我用的是一台配備 16GB RAM 的 MacBook Air M5。對這類工作負載來說，它大概不是最強的機器，但拿來跑低於 70 億參數的模型已經夠用。

但在我升級到 Ollama 新的 MLX 引擎後，情況完全改變了。我看到效能有非常明顯的提升。整體反應變得流暢許多，推論速度現在也幾乎快了一倍。

如果你已經透過 Ollama 在 Mac 上[執行本機 LLM](https://www.xda-developers.com/tested-local-llm-different-tools-and-only-one-unleashed-its-potential/)，這會是 Apple Silicon 成為認真可用的推論平台以來，最重要的升級之一。最新的 MLX 引擎改變了模型的表示方式、記憶體的使用方式，以及 agent 工作流程的快取方式，這也會大幅影響 [Claude Code 這類程式助理](https://www.xda-developers.com/found-a-free-open-source-alternative-to-claude-code/)，以及 OpenClaw、Aider 和其他多 agent 配置。

#### [我終於找到一個真的想拿來寫程式的本機 LLM](https://www.xda-developers.com/finally-found-local-llm-want-use-coding/)

Qwen3-Coder-Next 是一個很棒的模型，搭配 Claude Code 作為操作框架後表現更好。

## MLX 引擎終於能更好地發揮 Apple Silicon

### 它讓 Apple Silicon 物盡其用

多數本機 LLM 使用者應該都知道，Apple Silicon 雖然硬體規格相對不算誇張，但表現意外地好。我的 MacBook Air M5 配備 16GB RAM，處理較小的模型時沒有太多問題，但使用體驗總是伴隨一些取捨。執行本機模型時，經常會拖慢系統上的其他所有操作。

Ollama 新的 MLX 引擎改變了這一點，因為它更加依賴 Apple 自家的 MLX 框架與統一記憶體架構。你也知道，Apple Silicon 讓 CPU 和 GPU 可以共用同一個記憶體池，而不是把它們當成彼此分離的硬體。更新後的引擎更充分利用了這項設計，在推論期間減少不必要的記憶體搬移。

這些改進不只是更好的記憶體管理。Ollama 現在會透過 MLX 的即時編譯器（just-in-time compiler），把多個 GPU 操作合併成更大的 Metal kernel，降低推論開銷。這個引擎也改善了 GPU 加速的取樣，讓 token 產生速度比以前快得多。Ollama 聲稱，更新後的引擎輸出速度大約比先前的 Q4_K_M 實作高出 20%，這和我日常使用時注意到的情況相符。

我自己的工作流程從來不是圍繞著大型基準測試 prompt。大多數時候，我是在問程式問題、產生腳本，或測試自動化點子。這些工作負載是一天當中很多次短請求組成的，而現在每一次都感覺更即時。

## 較小的模型現在能產生更好的回應

### 終於

效能改進通常最受關注，但我認為品質上的改進同樣重要。Ollama 更新後的 MLX 引擎現在支援 NVIDIA 針對模型最佳化的 NVFP4 量化格式。量化會降低執行模型所需的記憶體，但也會從原始權重中移除一些資訊。記憶體用量降低，通常會以輸出品質下降作為代價。

NVFP4 大幅降低了這個取捨。根據 Ollama 自己用 Gemma 4 12B 進行的測量，和廣泛使用的 Q4_K_M 格式相比，新格式在記憶體需求相近的情況下，讓品質損失大約減少一半。基準測試顯示它的困惑度低於 Q4_K_M，這通常表示模型的表現更接近原本的 BF16 版本。

我的 Mac 沒辦法舒服地執行極大型模型，所以我大多數時間都在使用較小的模型。更好的量化讓較小模型不需要額外硬體，就能產生更強的結果。對於使用 MacBook Air，或其他記憶體有限的 Apple Silicon 系統的人來說，這是很有意義的升級。

我現在注意到，產生出來的程式碼更能穩定遵循指令，而且後續 prompt 需要修正的次數也比以前少。回應在較長對話中也能維持連貫，減少我重寫 prompt 所花的時間。

## 寫程式代理受益更大

### Ollama 重新設計了代理工作流程

最讓我意外的功能，其實跟原始推論速度無關。Ollama 也重新設計了 MLX 引擎在代理工作流程中處理快取模型狀態的方式。這很重要，因為程式碼助理會不斷把大量上下文重新送回模型。每一次工具呼叫都包含系統提示、工具定義、先前的對話紀錄，以及最近載入的檔案。

### Mac 效能升級也能省：加速 AI 工作流程的優惠

傳統的前綴快取只在每個請求都直接延續前一個請求時才有效。現代程式碼代理很少這樣運作，因為它們經常分支到子代理、重試失敗的請求，或把推理 token 從可見的對話中移除。這些變動通常會迫使模型一再處理相同的上下文，即使其中大部分內容根本沒有改變。

Ollama 透過新的快照系統解決這個問題。引擎不再完全依賴前綴快取，而是在對話的重要節點儲存可重複使用的模型狀態。不同的代理工作階段可以從這些已儲存的狀態接續，而不必從頭重建一切。思考型模型也會受益，因為快照會在推理 token 從對話紀錄中消失之前，保留有用的狀態。

### Ollama 現在好用多了

這次更新改善了你使用本機 LLM 的各種情境，不論是跟模型聊天，還是把它當成程式碼助理使用。我自己的本機工作流程感覺快了許多，因為重複的工具呼叫不再花那麼多時間重建上下文。更快的回應時間，加上更好的輸出品質，讓新的 MLX 引擎成為我對本機 AI 設定所做過最值得的升級之一。

#### Ollama

Ollama 是一個可以在你的本機電腦上下載並執行各種開源大型語言模型（LLM）的平台。

#### [Ollama 仍然是開始使用本機 LLM 最簡單的方式，但也是最不適合長期持續執行的方式](https://www.xda-developers.com/ollama-easiest-way-start-local-llms-worst-keep-running/)

Ollama 很適合帶你入門……只是不要一直留在這裡。

- [AI 工具](https://www.xda-developers.com/ai-tools/)
- [AI](https://www.xda-developers.com/tag/ai/)

#### [我讓 Gemma 4 和 Qwen 3.5 跑同一批本機任務，結果其中一個遙遙領先](https://www.xda-developers.com/ran-gemma-4-and-qwen-35-for-same-local-tasks-one-pulled-ahead/)

#### [我救回來的兩張老 GPU，做的 AI 工作比一張全新 2,000 美元顯卡還多，而且我短期內不打算升級](https://www.xda-developers.com/two-old-gpus-are-doing-more-ai-work-than-a-brand-new-card/)

#### [高 VRAM 顯卡不是本機 AI 的未來，統一記憶體與 Mixture of Experts（混合專家）模型才是](https://www.xda-developers.com/high-vram-gpus-future-local-ai-unified-memory-mixture-experts/)

我現在注意到，產生出來的程式碼更能穩定遵循指令，而且後續 prompt 需要修正的次數也比以前少。回應在較長對話中也能維持連貫，減少我重寫 prompt 所花的時間。

## 寫程式代理受益更大

### Ollama 重新設計了代理工作流程

最讓我意外的功能，其實跟原始推論速度無關。Ollama 也重新設計了 MLX 引擎在代理工作流程中處理快取模型狀態的方式。這很重要，因為程式碼助理會不斷把大量上下文重新送回模型。每一次工具呼叫都包含系統提示、工具定義、先前的對話紀錄，以及最近載入的檔案。

### Mac 效能升級也能省：加速 AI 工作流程的優惠

傳統的前綴快取只在每個請求都直接延續前一個請求時才有效。現代程式碼代理很少這樣運作，因為它們經常分支到子代理、重試失敗的請求，或把推理 token 從可見的對話中移除。這些變動通常會迫使模型一再處理相同的上下文，即使其中大部分內容根本沒有改變。

Ollama 透過新的快照系統解決這個問題。引擎不再完全依賴前綴快取，而是在對話的重要節點儲存可重複使用的模型狀態。不同的代理工作階段可以從這些已儲存的狀態接續，而不必從頭重建一切。思考型模型也會受益，因為快照會在推理 token 從對話紀錄中消失之前，保留有用的狀態。

### Ollama 現在好用多了

這次更新改善了你使用本機 LLM 的各種情境，不論是跟模型聊天，還是把它當成程式碼助理使用。我自己的本機工作流程感覺快了許多，因為重複的工具呼叫不再花那麼多時間重建上下文。更快的回應時間，加上更好的輸出品質，讓新的 MLX 引擎成為我對本機 AI 設定所做過最值得的升級之一。
